key_insight: A diagnosis-adapted multi-expert language-model framework improved 180-day opioid overdose risk prediction from prior-year ICD histories.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help identify higher-risk patients earlier and more precisely, supporting targeted overdose prevention efforts in health systems.
method: Continued pretraining on longitudinal diagnosis sequences, then task-specific fine-tuning
Built two diagnosis-adapted models: OODMAMBA and OODQWEN
Combined multiple model scales in OVERDOSEMOE using expert-weighting strategies
evidence_signal: In the abstract, OODQWEN reached AUPRC 24.47 and AUROC 68.56, while OVERDOSEMOE improved to AUPRC 25.17 and AUROC 69.49, with external validation on MIMIC-IV.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on retrospective EHR data, so real-world deployment would still require careful calibration, bias checks, and prospective validation.
paper_title: OverdoseMoE: A Multi-Expert Framework for Opioid Overdose Risk Prediction
